Breakdown.theorem71_extended.summary: From a certificate in the sense of §7.3 it gives one $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ and a smooth nonzero profile of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry whose correction $v=W(S\theta,\cdot)-W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha$ satisfies (7.38), with the symmetries (7.39). Proved from the authors' library.
Breakdown.theorem71_extended.note:
This is our own statement of Theorem 7.1, written to keep everything the paper's theorem asserts about the chosen parameter. Assume a certificate in the formal sense of §7.3. The formal statement gives one parameter $\alpha$ in the parameter set and a pair $(W,q)$ that is jointly smooth, solves the profile equation (1.2) with period $S(\alpha)>0$ and the identity isometry, is divergence free and not identically zero, and obeys $|
abla^jW(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-1-j}$ for $j=0,1,2$ and $|
abla q(s,y)|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. For the correction $v(	heta,y)=W(S	heta,y)-W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha(	heta,y)$ it gives membership in the perturbation class $\mathcal D^\Gamma_S$, the bound $\|v\|_w^2+\omega^2| eta^{\mathrm a}(\alpha)|^2\le4\varepsilon^2$, the bound $\sup_	heta\|v(	heta)\|_{\dot H^1}\le M$ and the pin values $\ell(v)= ar\ell(\alpha)$, which are the three parts of (7.38). It also gives $W(s+	heta_0S,Ry)=RW(s,y)$ for every $(R,	heta_0)\in\Gamma$, which is (7.39) after replacing $y$ by $Ry$. The weighted norm is stated together with the finiteness of its integrand, and matrix norms are Frobenius norms. Compared with the paper, the conclusion asserts more about the profile (decay of $
abla^2W$ and of $
abla q$), and the hypothesis is the formal certificate, which asks for more regularity of the approximate profiles than §7.3 does. The authors' own formal Theorem 7.1 concludes only that some weak profile exists; this statement keeps the parameter, the period, the correction and its bounds.

Breakdown.theorem71_cell.summary: From data meeting the fifteen groups of cell conditions of Appendix B it gives the same conclusion as our Theorem 7.1, for the certificate that the cell data form: one parameter, a smooth nonzero profile, (7.38) and (7.39).
Breakdown.theorem71_cell.note:
This is our statement of the conclusion of Theorem 7.1 for the certificate assembled from cell data, the route of Proposition B.14. Assume data of the form of Appendix B.1 meeting all fifteen groups of cell conditions. The formal statement gives, for the certificate those data form, one parameter $\alpha$ and a smooth nonzero profile $(W,q)$ of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry with the decay bounds on $W$, $
abla W$, $
abla^2W$ and $
abla q$, whose correction satisfies the three bounds of (7.38) and whose symmetries are (7.39). It combines Proposition B.14 (the cell data are a certificate) with our Theorem 7.1. It does not assert that any concrete data meet the cell conditions; the certificate data and their interval-arithmetic check are outside the formalisation.

Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.title: The conclusion of Theorem 7.1
Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.source:
def ExtendedConclusion {k : ℕ} (d : ExtendedCertificateData k) : Prop :=
  ∃ α ∈ d.params, ∃ (W : ℝ → Space → Space) (q : ℝ → Space → ℝ),
    IsIdentityProfile (d.period α) W q ∧
    CorrectionBounds d.symmetries (d.period α) (d.profile α)
      d.multiplierWeight (d.multiplier α) d.pin (d.targetGap α)
      d.weightFn d.sizeBound d.supBound W ∧
    PrescribedSymmetries d.symmetries (d.period α) W
Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.summary: The conclusion of Theorem 7.1 for one certificate: some $\alpha\in\mathcal K$ and a smooth nonzero profile of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry whose correction satisfies (7.38) and whose symmetries are (7.39).
Breakdown.Theorem71.ExtendedConclusion.note:
For a certificate, this proposition asserts that there are a parameter $\alpha$ in the parameter set and a pair $(W,q)$ with three properties. First, $(W,q)$ is a smooth nonzero profile with period $S(\alpha)$ and the identity isometry, with decay of $W$, $
abla W$, $
abla^2W$ and $
abla q$. Second, the correction $v=W(S	heta,\cdot)-W^{\mathrm a}_\alpha$ lies in the perturbation class and satisfies the weighted bound, the uniform $\dot H^1$ bound and the pin values of (7.38). Third, $W$ has every symmetry prescribed by $\Gamma$, as in (7.39). It is a definition of what Theorem 7.1 asserts, used by our two statements above.

comparisons.note: Theorem 7.1 gives one $\alpha$, a profile of period $S(\alpha)$ and identity isometry, (7.38) for the correction and the symmetries (7.39). Our formal statement gives all of these for the same $\alpha$ and the same profile, and adds decay of $\nabla^2W$ and $\nabla q$; its hypothesis is the formal certificate, which asks for more regularity of the approximate profiles than §7.3. So the conclusion is at least as strong and the hypothesis is the formal one.

Our formal statement keeps the chosen parameter, the period, the correction and the three bounds of (7.38) with the symmetries (7.39), and adds decay of $\nabla^2W$ and $\nabla q$; it assumes the formal certificate, which asks for more regularity than §7.3.

The sentence combines Proposition B.14 with Theorem 7.1 and Corollary 7.2. Our formal statement combines the cell conditions with Theorem 7.1 and keeps the profile with (7.38) and (7.39); it stops before Corollary 7.2, whose formal form is the nonexistence statement tied to this sentence.

transposeApply.question: Why did Comparator reject the standalone readable cell file against the library on one definition?
transposeApply.answer: The two definitions elaborate to the same type and the same value except for the name of one auxiliary proof: the proof that 1 + 1 is at least two, inside the numeral 2 that is the exponent of the Euclidean space. Lean stores that proof as an auxiliary theorem named after the first declaration of its module, so it is named differently in the two files. Renaming it makes the two constants identical. A second comparison of all 1,923 library constants used by the statements of the three cell theorems, with auxiliary proofs identified by their statements, found every one identical. No mathematical statement differs.
